newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says no plans for Golan oil drilling.
newsitem.headline: Israel says no plans for Golan oil drilling.

text.p: Israel said on Sunday it had no plans to drill for oil on the Golan Heights, following a news report that angered Syria and irritated France.
Israel's National Infrastructure Ministry said plans by its state-owned National Oil Company for new drilling were cancelled because of a government decision to privatise the firm.
An official Syrian newspaper on Saturday blasted Israel's prime minister over an Israeli news report of his plans for the heights captured from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war.
"The National Oil Company has a concession for oil searches in the Golan Heights and in the past there were indeed plans for drilling in this strip of land," the ministry said on Sunday.
"Insofar as, based on a government decision, the National Oil Company is facing privatisation, the plans for new drilling were cancelled, including the plans for drilling on the Golan Heights."
Israel's Haaretz newspaper said on Friday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had approved a company request to drill for oil on the heights.
Syria's Tishreen newspaper had said the Israeli decision was a "blunt threat" to peace in the Middle East. Damascus demands a full Israeli withdrawal from the heights.
Israel's previous government, ousted by Netanyahu in May elections, was ready to make at least a partial withdrawal for full peace and normal ties with Syria.
Netanyahu rejects trading occupied Arab land for peace.

Asked about the report, French President Jacques Chirac said in Beirut on Friday: "I don't think it was particularly well chosen to take this initiative but perhaps Mr Netanyahu has reasons to think otherwise."
